laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: To drive in Macau, you need both: - a valid international driving permit (IDP) - your current Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted) If you stay in Macau longer than 14 days, you must register your driving licence with the Macau Public Security Police Force (CPSP). Get your IDP in Australia before you leave. You may not be covered by your travel and vehicle insurances if you drive without an IDP.
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Arriving with cash or cash-like bearer instruments worth MOP 120,000 or more means using the Red Channel with a completed declaration form. When leaving, you must say truthfully how much cash you carry if a Customs officer asks. Customs also expects dutiable goods over the duty-free quota to be declared.
laws.penalty_signal: Not disclosing truthfully on leaving: a fine of MOP 1,000 to MOP 500,000.

laws.rule: Macau bans smoking in indoor public places except authorised casino and airport smoking lounges, and outdoors in public parks and gardens, public beaches, footbridges, underpasses and within 10 metres of public bus stops. News reports put the fixed penalty for smoking illegally at MOP 1,500. The Health Bureau page could not be read, so confirm with the Health Bureau (SSM).

citizenship.summary: Official naturalisation, descent and dual-citizenship rules in Macau, for an Australian passport holder.

facts.label: Dual citizenship (destination rule)
facts.text: Whether the destination allows dual citizenship should be confirmed on the official nationality pages. Do not assume that a residence permit leads to citizenship, or that Australia's rule applies there.

facts.label: Citizenship by descent
facts.text: Many countries have a descent route with official documentary conditions. Confirm eligibility on the official nationality pages before planning around it.

facts.label: Official authority
facts.text: Start with Identification Services Bureau for official naturalisation, descent and dual-citizenship rules.

citizenship.notes: Australian law also matters: Australia allows its citizens to hold another citizenship. That does not change the destination country's own dual-citizenship rules.
